kept: a reference's identity is its normal form: its sheet, its shape and each coordinate as absolute or relative to the caller, not its source spelling

changes.change: The identity is the typed value ReferenceOperand (SheetTarget, ReferenceShape, AxisRef), compared and hashed as a value, instead of a String formatted from a profile name, workbook and sheet id strings and R/C axis text.
changes.reason: The Do asks for typed operands and the Port-from line for Excel semantics, not profiles; a key built from text is a constructed address string. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute: =B3+$B3+B$3+$B$3 bound at C5, =E8+$B8+E$3+$B$3 bound at F10 and =R[-2]C[-1]+R[-2]C2+R3C[-1]+R3C2 bound at C5 and at F10 give equal operands, and =B3 bound at F10 does not.

changes.change: An unqualified reference's sheet is SheetTarget::Anchor, taken from the anchor when the operand is placed, not the caller's sheet id written into the key at binding.
changes.reason: A formula copied to another sheet reads that sheet. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute: Sheet2!B3 and B3 bound at Sheet1!C5 and placed at Sheet3!F10 give Sheet2!E8 and Sheet3!E8.

kept: the identity of a reference excludes the caller anchor; the anchor is supplied when the reference is placed

changes.change: No policy enum: an operand never holds an anchor, and ReferenceOperand::instantiate takes one.
changes.reason: There is one behaviour, Excel's. The enum itself, for plan and template keys, is listed in the Port-from lines of cfml-m1.3 and cfml-m2.1; see not_ported.

kept: a reference that no placement puts on the grid is refused when it is bound
a reference whose placement leaves the grid is #REF! at that placement

changes.change: Placement validity is not stored with the bound reference: instantiate returns PlacementError::RowOffGrid or PlacementError::ColumnOffGrid, with the coordinate reached, at an anchor where the operand leaves the grid, and worksheet_error gives #REF!.
changes.reason: One operand is valid at one anchor and not at another. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute: nine off-grid placements, each #REF!, and the same operands one step inside the grid placing.

kept: binding asks a provider that owns the workbook's identities

changes.change: The provider receives a sheet name (catalogue) or a GridArea (reader), never source text, a parsed qualifier string or caller coordinates.
changes.reason: The Acceptance case cfml_m1_2__provider_reads: an independently instrumented provider sees typed requests, not constructed address strings. Witnessed there: the catalogue's log is exactly [sheet2, Q2 Data, It's, Sheet2, Missing] and the reader's log five GridAreas.

sources.clean_replacements: The file takes value types (CalcValue, ReferenceLike, WorksheetErrorCode, ExcelText) from oxfunc_core::value and its provider interface (ReferenceSystemProvider and its requests) from oxfunc_core::resolver. The port uses calc-value's types through calc_func::value (cfunc-m0.1) for the first and ReferenceCatalog and ReferenceReader, written fresh in calc-fml, for the second. No code of the file, and nothing it takes from oxfunc_core, is copied; the entries below re-implement the Excel behaviour of its two named symbols.

ported.to: crates/calc-fml/src/reference/bind.rs bind_references, Binder::walk, Binder::qualified, Binder::lone, Binder::range, Binder::spell, qualifier_of
kept: A1 and R1C1 notation each read by their own rules, chosen per formula (FormulaChannelKind::WorksheetR1C1 becomes ReferenceNotation::R1C1)
Excel's grid of 1048576 rows by 16384 columns (calc-value MAX_ROWS and MAX_COLUMNS)
a qualified reference binds to the qualifier's sheet

changes.change: A qualifier naming another workbook is refused with BindError::ExternalWorkbook. The pinned bind_range bound an external whole-axis range ([Book2]Sheet1!A:A) as a host-sensitive record.
changes.reason: External references are cfml-m3.5's; the refusal is typed at the site, not a substitute. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__provider_reads ([Book2.xlsx]Sheet1!A1, and no catalogue request for it).

changes.change: A run of sheets (Sheet1:Sheet3!A1, 'Sheet 1:Sheet 3'!A1) is refused with BindError::SheetSpan; the pinned profile bound 3D spans.
changes.reason: 3D spans are cfml-m3.2's. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__provider_reads.

changes.change: A qualifier that names no sheet of the catalogue is refused with BindError::UnknownSheet; the pinned profile wrote the qualifier text into the record as the sheet id without resolving it.
changes.reason: A sheet is a SheetId the catalogue gives. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__provider_reads (Missing!A1).

changes.change: #REF!A1 binds to SheetTarget::Deleted, and placing it gives PlacementError::DeletedSheet (#REF!).
changes.reason: cfml-m1.1's parser keeps #REF!A1 as a qualified reference, and the claim note asks for the #REF! qualifier as a typed #REF! result. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute (#REF!B3 and #REF!$B$3:C4 placed at C5 and F10).

changes.change: A qualifier is read as another workbook's when it is a bracketed qualifier or its name holds [, ], \ or /, as a run of sheets when its name holds :, and otherwise as one sheet's name for the catalogue (qualifier_of).
changes.reason: Excel does not allow those characters in a sheet name, so a name holding one cannot be a single sheet. Not measured against Excel by this bead: the character test itself, including how Excel reads a quoted qualifier such as 'C:\[B.xlsx]S'!B3 or 'S 1:S 2'!B3. Witnessed by reference::bind::tests::qualifiers_and_refusals and cfml_m1_2__provider_reads ('Sheet 1:Sheet 3'!A1).

changes.change: A qualifier (one sheet, a run of sheets, another workbook or #REF!) applies to its whole operand, which binds with the qualifier or is refused: before an operand that is no reference endpoint and no name (Sheet2!(A1), [Book2.xlsx]Sheet1!(A1), Sheet1:Sheet3!(A1), Nope!(A1), Sheet2!Sheet3!A1, #REF!SUM(A1), Sheet2!SUM(A1), Sheet2!3, Sheet2!#REF!) it is one BindError::QualifiedNonReference site, and the catalogue is not asked. A qualified name (Sheet2!TaxRate) gives no site.
changes.reason: The round-1 walk entered such an operand and bound the reference inside it as unqualified, a hidden fallback onto the anchor's sheet (honesty rule 2). Not measured against Excel by this bead: whether Excel accepts any of these forms. Sheet2!#REF! is the form Excel writes for a deleted cell; it is refused here, not modelled. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__provider_reads (each formula gives exactly that one refused site and the catalogue log does not grow).

changes.change: Syntax the parser refused (an UnsupportedExpr: a trim reference such as Sheet1!A1.:B10, a . member selector such as (A1).Value) is one BindError::UnsupportedSyntax site, and no reference inside it is bound.
changes.reason: Binding the parts of a refused trim range or selector as ordinary references would give them a meaning the parser refused. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__provider_reads (=SUM(Sheet1!A1.:B10)+C1 and =(A1).Value+C1 each give the refused site and C1).

ported.to: crates/calc-fml/src/reference/read.rs ReferenceReader, CellRun, read_cells; crates/calc-fml/src/reference/mod.rs ReferenceOperand::instantiate, AxisRef::at
kept: a relative axis lands at the caller's coordinate plus its offset, and outside 1 to the grid's size it names no cell
a cell the provider cannot supply is never read as a blank cell (the pinned provider's unrouted-sheet rule)
a whole-row or whole-column read does not produce every blank cell

changes.change: Values come through ReferenceReader::read_area as row-major CellRuns: values borrowed from the reader's storage, counts of blank cells and counts of missing cells. The pinned provider returned cloned values (dereference) or the defined cells of a sparse extent (enumerate_values) from BTreeMap<ExcelGridCellAddress, CalcValue> maps keyed by workbook and sheet id strings.
changes.reason: The Do: a reader returning borrowed, chunked values with missing and blank kept apart, and no BTreeMap<String,...> providers. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__provider_reads: values arrive at the reader's own storage addresses, and Sheet2!B:B arrives in five runs covering 1048576 cells.

changes.change: A cell the reader cannot supply is CellRun::Missing. The pinned provider turned every cell of an unrouted sheet into the #REF! value; which worksheet value evaluation gives a missing cell is not decided by this bead.
changes.reason: The reader reports what it holds; the result of an unsupplied input belongs to evaluation (cfml-m1.3). Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__provider_reads: Sheet2!C3 and It's!B3 are Missing, Sheet2!B3 and Sheet1!B4 Blank.

changes.change: read_cells checks that a reader's runs cover the requested area exactly, and returns ReadContractError when they do not.
changes.reason: Blank cardinality (plan section 4.2) would otherwise rest on each reader. Witnessed by the calc-fml unit tests reference::read::tests::too_few_or_too_many_cells_break_the_contract and a_stopped_read_is_not_short.

changes.change: Placing an operand whose relative row or column lands off the grid is PlacementError::RowOffGrid or ColumnOffGrid, the worksheet value #REF!, in A1 and in R1C1 alike (=R[-1]C placed at row 1, D7 entered in C5 placed at XFD1048576).
changes.reason: The pinned provider named no cell off the grid, which this keeps as a typed refusal. Not measured against Excel by this bead: Excel may wrap a relative reference around the grid on some routes (copying, filling or R1C1 entry) instead of giving #REF!, and no capture of this bead decides which route does what. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute (nine off-grid placements, each #REF!).

ported.symbol: parse_a1_cell_reference, parse_a1_row_axis_fragment, parse_a1_col_axis_fragment, strip_optional_dollar, column_to_index, axis_delta
kept: [$]letters[$]digits is a cell, [$]digits a row and [$]letters a column; a $ makes the axis after it absolute
column letters in either case, A being 1
a relative A1 coordinate becomes its offset from the caller's
a fixed coordinate outside the grid is refused ($XFE$1, 1:1048577, $XFE:$XFE)

changes.change: A cell or column form without a $ that lies outside the grid (XFE1, Sales2023, A0, XFE:XFE) is not a reference; binding leaves it to name binding. The pinned parser refused it as outside the grid.
changes.reason: Excel names such as Sales2023 have the letters-then-digits form, so refusing every such text outside the grid refuses valid names; a form with a $ cannot be a name and stays refused. Not measured against Excel by this bead: that Excel reads cell-like text outside the grid (XFE1, Sales2023, A0, XFE:XFE) as a name. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute (=XFE1+Sales2023+A0+XFE:XFE binds no site; the five $ and row forms are refused) and reference::notation::tests::a1_forms_at_an_anchor.

changes.change: A row endpoint is a number token (1:3) or an identifier ($1), and a lone row or column is not a reference in A1 notation.
changes.reason: cfml-m1.1's parser presents 1:3 as two number literals and $1 as an identifier; A1 notation has no lone row or column reference. Witnessed by reference::bind::tests::ranges_bind_as_one_reference_only_between_endpoints_of_one_form_and_sheet.

kept: R and C each followed by nothing (the caller's own row or column), a 1-based number or a bracketed signed offset
an absolute R1C1 coordinate outside the grid is refused
a bracketed offset may carry a + sign (R[+2]C reads as R[2]C), as the pinned parser's i32 parse accepted. Not measured against Excel by this bead. Witnessed by reference::notation::tests::r1c1_forms.

changes.change: R and C are read in either case.
changes.reason: The pinned parser read upper case only; lower-case r and c (r3c2) are read here as Excel's English R1C1 entry is taken to read them. Not measured against Excel by this bead. Witnessed by reference::notation::tests::r1c1_forms.

changes.change: A bracketed offset as long as the grid or longer (R[1048576]C, C[-16384]) is refused at binding with BindError::OutsideGrid; the pinned parser bound any i32 offset and marked it invalid for the current placement.
changes.reason: No caller puts such an offset on the grid. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute: R[1048576]C is refused, and R[-1048575]C binds and places only at the last row.

changes.change: A lone R1C1 row (R3, R[1], R) or column (C2, C[1], C) is a whole-row or whole-column reference; the pinned parser read lone R1C1 axes only as range endpoints.
changes.reason: Excel's R1C1 notation names whole rows and columns this way. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute: R and C bound at C5 and placed at F10 give row 10 and column F.

ported.symbol: whole_row_range_reference, whole_column_range_reference, canonical_axis_pair, axis_resolved_for_order, parsed_axis_pair, range_sheet_id, axis_valid_for_current_placement, range_axis_validity
ported.to: crates/calc-fml/src/reference/bind.rs Binder::range, pair, ordered; crates/calc-fml/src/reference/mod.rs ReferenceOperand::instantiate
kept: two row endpoints make whole rows and two column endpoints whole columns
both endpoints lie on one sheet

changes.change: Each pair of ends (an area's rows and columns, a run of rows or of columns) is held in an order that no anchor changes: two absolute or two relative coordinates by position, an absolute and a relative one absolute first (ordered). The pinned canonical_axis_pair ordered each pair by its position at the binding caller (axis_resolved_for_order). Placing the operand orders the corners on the grid.
changes.reason: An operand's identity must not depend on the anchor it was bound at: ordered at the caller, R[-2]C[-1]:R7C4 bound at C5 and at F10 gave two unequal operands. The pinned legacy expectations ($A:C as Absolute(1), Relative(-2); C:A as Relative(-4), Relative(-2)) hold under this order. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute (R[-2]C[-1]:R7C4+R[-3]:R4 bound at C5 equals the same bound at F10 and B3:$D$7+2:$4, $D$7:B3+$4:2, E8:$D$7+7:$4 and $D$7:E8+$4:7 at their callers, and places as B3:D7 and rows 2:4 at C5, D7:E8 and rows 4:7 at F10) and reference::bind::tests::endpoints_are_ordered_per_axis_without_the_anchor.

changes.change: Two cell endpoints make one rectangle (ReferenceShape::Area), ordered per axis like the whole-axis pairs; the pinned profile left A1:B2 as a range-operator composition of two cell references.
changes.reason: The Do: cell and rectangular references. Witnessed by cfml_m1_2__relative_absolute (B3:$D$7 placed at C5 and F10) and reference::bind::tests::endpoints_are_ordered_per_axis_without_the_anchor.

changes.change: One sheet is decided by the catalogue's SheetId (Sheet2!B3:sheet2!D7 is one area), not by comparing sheet id strings; endpoints on two sheets, or an unqualified endpoint before a qualified one, are the range operator between two separately bound references.
changes.reason: Sheet names match regardless of case, and the range operator between separate references is cfml-m3.3's. Witnessed by reference::bind::tests::ranges_bind_as_one_reference_only_between_endpoints_of_one_form_and_sheet.

ported.symbol: ExcelGridAxisRef (Absolute(u32), Relative(i32)) and ExcelGridReferenceStyle (A1, R1C1), as parse.rs and reference_engine.rs use them

owner_search.rule: The beads of each not_ported entry are the beads the pin lists for the item's input (cfml-m1.2, cfml-m3.1, cfml-m3.2, cfml-m3.3, cfml-m3.5, cfml-m4.1 and cfml-m4.2 for the four OxCalc files; those and cfml-m1.3, cfml-m2.1, cfml-m2.2, cfml-m2.3, cfml-m3.4, cfml-m4.3, cfml-m5.1, onecalc-m1.1, onecalc-m2.1 and onecalc-m8.1 for profile.rs) whose Do in docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md names the item's job, read bead by bead, plus the beads that grep -n -i -E "render|reconstruct|dependency fact" docs/plan/BEAD_DETAILS.md finds for rendering and dependency facts.
owner_search.inputs: The pinned inputs assigned to cfml-m1.2 are the five entries of migration/source-manifest.json whose beads include cfml-m1.2: profile.rs, reference_engine.rs, parse.rs, profile_codec.rs and transform.rs. Each was looked up with cargo xtask pin-sources --lookup; the exits and calls_quarantined lists here come from those transcripts.
owner_search.legacy_tests: Test names are the #[test] functions of each pinned blob. profile.rs, parse.rs, profile_codec.rs and transform.rs hold none; reference_engine.rs holds 52, each listed below. Owners are found by the rule above.

tests.reason: =R[-1]C bound at row 1 binds without a refusal, and placing it at that anchor is PlacementError::RowOffGrid.
The target sheet is the catalogue's SheetId instead of the qualifier text.
A blank cell of a sheet the reader holds is CellRun::Blank (Sheet2!B3); the routed-sheet scope builder is not ported, since a reader answers for any sheet it holds.
The A1 offsets are kept (=B3 bound at F10 gives offsets -7 and -4); the rebind and reuse flags of incremental binding are dropped for cfml-m2.5 and cfml-m2.1.
=XFE1 binds no site (a name); $XFE$1 is refused with BindError::OutsideGrid. See the parse.rs changes.
=XFE:XFE binds no site (names); $XFE:$XFE is refused with BindError::OutsideGrid.
A1:B2 binds as one ReferenceShape::Area operand.
External references are refused with BindError::ExternalWorkbook until cfml-m3.5 binds them.
Every 3D span is refused with BindError::SheetSpan, with no capability flag, until cfml-m3.2 binds them.
A bound cell's value is read through read_cells as a borrowed value, not dereferenced as a clone.
A cell the reader cannot supply is CellRun::Missing, never Blank; the #REF! value the pinned provider gave it is left to evaluation (cfml-m1.3).
A whole-axis read arrives as runs whose blank counts cover the extent (exercised on Sheet2!B:B, a whole column).
B2:B4 binds as one area and reads as runs; composition by the range operator is cfml-m3.3's.
Text resolution, union, spill and INDIRECT of names.
Evaluation of a function over a read area.
Defined names.
Structured references.
Binding 3D sheet spans.
Sheet deletion inside 3D spans.
Structural and sheet-lifecycle transforms.
Editor reference information.
Profile records and routing by reference system; a reader receives grid areas only.
